source.description: Project HTTP parser source point where the attacker-controlled request buffer is loaded from helper state.

sink.description: Out-of-bounds one-byte READ while testing whitespace on a cursor that has reached beyond the valid request buffer.

root_cause.description: The parser calls ignore_leading_whitespace on the request buffer without first enforcing a minimum request size or checking that the cursor remains far enough inside the buffer.

taint_source.description: Unscored fuzzing boundary; the scored source is parse_http_request loading helper->buffer.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled request bytes are used as the parser cursor.

coarse_trace.summary: The HTTP parser loads the attacker-controlled request buffer and immediately trims leading whitespace.
A byte-wise whitespace scan reads past the valid buffer when no minimum request length/bound is enforced.

root_cause_analysis.summary: The attacker controls the HTTP request buffer and can provide a very short or whitespace-only request. parse_http_request loads the buffer and calls ignore_leading_whitespace before validating that the request has the minimum length required for parsing or that the returned cursor remains safely inside the buffer. ignore_leading_whitespace performs byte-by-byte dereferences while advancing the cursor, so a malformed short input can make the loop read one byte beyond the valid buffer.
root_cause_analysis.why_patch_works: The patch introduces `min_request_size`, rejects buffers shorter than a minimal HTTP request, and checks after ignore_leading_whitespace that the cursor still leaves enough bytes for a valid request. These guards prevent the whitespace scanner and subsequent parser stages from operating on an under-sized request buffer.
